answer: Reputation Inlet Cooldown. Each new identity may only submit work through a metered inlet: its first N actions earn near-zero payout while outcomes are verified against a random sample. A hollow account therefore pays full compute and latency cost but recovers only a fraction of value, since reward is withheld until the sample confirms honest behavior. Repeated clone creation compounds this loss, and the copper-weighted audit fee per sampled unit stays charged whether or not the identity survives, making every marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
